title: Distributed Tracing and OpenTelemetry
description: Learn how distributed tracing works and how OpenTelemetry provides a vendor-neutral instrumentation standard.

data.text: Distributed tracing tracks a request as it flows through multiple services in a microservices architecture. Each service adds a span -- a named unit of work with a start time, end time, and attributes. The collection of spans forms a trace that shows the full journey of the request.

terms.definition: The complete path of a single request across all services.
A single operation within a trace, such as an HTTP call or database query.
A unique identifier shared by all spans in a single trace.
A unique identifier for a single span within a trace.
The ID of the span that triggered the current span, forming a tree.

data.text: OpenTelemetry (OTel) is an open-source observability framework that provides a standard way to instrument applications. Instead of learning a vendor-specific SDK, you instrument once with OTel and export data to any backend: Azure Monitor, Jaeger, Prometheus, Datadog, and more.

data.title: Azure Support for OpenTelemetry
data.text: Azure Monitor supports OpenTelemetry via the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter. You can instrument your app with OTel and send traces directly to Azure Monitor without using the Application Insights SDK.

data.title: Generate a Distributed Trace
data.description: Instrument a multi-service app to produce a correlated trace.
steps: Create two Express services: orders and inventory.
Have the orders service call the inventory service via HTTP.
View the trace in Jaeger or Azure Monitor.
